extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers; employers, labor unions, and wage/price stabilization and administration officials
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report summarizing new Office of Stabilization/Price Administration regulations and standards governing wage and salary adjustments, pre-approval, price-relief treatment, and agency procedures. Intended to inform the public and affected employers/unions/administrators about what increases will be approved and what documentation and tests apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-approval by Stabilization Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-approval is granted by the Stabilization Administrator to wage or salary adjustments which are found by the appropriate stabilization agency's judgment the adjustment would be consistent with the stabilization program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes that the Stabilization Administrator can pre-approve adjustments; the determination is made in the judgment of the appropriate stabilization agency. (Text: “PRE-APPROVAL IS GRANTED BY THE STABILIZATION ADMINISTRATOR … TO WAGE OR SALARY ADJUSTMENTS WHICH ARE FOUND BY THE APPROPRIATE … AGENCY'S JUDGMENT THE ADJUSTMENT WOULD BE CONSISTENT WITH THE STABILIZATION PROGRAM.”)

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic approval for specified classes of adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Wage or salary adjustments falling within specified classes listed in the regulations are automatically approved as increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when automatically approved, applicants still must obtain approval from the stabilization agency; that approval may be taken into account in determining price or rent ceilings. When approval is obtained the employer may use these increases — as increased costs to the Government — as a basis for seeking increases in price ceilings or other price relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of preapproved increases (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations list specific classes of wage/salary adjustments that are preapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed classes include (as stated in the text): increases to compensate for rises in cost of living; increases to correct inequities in rates paid in different plants in the same industry or locality; increases under standards applied by the National War Labor Board which were in effect prior to August 18, 1945; increases lawfully made or approved by the appropriate wage or salary stabilization agency before August 18, 1945; increases made in accordance with the terms and conditions of a wage or salary schedule lawfully in effect before August 18, 1945; increases made in accordance with requirements of War Labor Board or Salary Stabilization Unit regulations regarding the institution of new piece rates or new job rates in line with existing piece or job rates; and increases made in accordance with existing orders of the War Labor Board regarding increases up to 35 cents an hour to correct substandards of living. (Guidance: these specific categories are enumerated by the regulations as preapproved classes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards guiding Office of Price Administration (OPA) on price-relief applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards are provided to guide the Office of Price Administration in dealing with applications for price relief under Executive Order 9651, specifically that unapproved wage-or-salary adjustments shall be taken into consideration in determining price or rent ceilings after a reasonable test period (generally six months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations require submission of an operating or financial statement to the Price Administrator reflecting the effect of the wage increase on costs or showing the employer's profit position for the test period. The test period is generally six months; after this period unapproved increases may be considered for price or rent ceiling adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirement for price relief consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An operating or financial statement must be submitted to the Price Administrator reflecting the effect of the wage increase on costs or showing the employer's profit position for the test period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement is required when seeking price relief; it must reflect the effect of the wage increase on costs or demonstrate the employer's profit position for the specified test period (generally six months). The OPA will use this information when deciding whether to adjust price or rent ceilings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of unapproved increases in price/rent-ceiling determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: An unapproved wage or salary increase may be considered as part of labor costs in determining whether a reduction in price or rent ceilings is justifiable, subject to timing and prior announcement by OPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unapproved increase may be included in labor costs for price/rent-ceiling decisions if the OPA had not announced that a reduction was under consideration at the time the wage or salary increase was made. Conversely, an unapproved increase may not warrant consequent increases in price or rent ceilings (or any particular amount) unless required under applicable maximum price/rent regulations or statutory/administrative standards governing changes in ceilings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency action restrictions and exceptions for proposed increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Wage or salary stabilization agencies shall not consider or act upon a proposed wage or salary increase in some circumstances, with limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations provide that agencies shall not act on certain proposed increases; however, this does not bar consideration of an increase which is contingent only on approval by the wage or salary stabilization agency, or of an increase which will not be put into effect until the Office of Price Administration has made a definite determination as to whether price relief is required. (Text clarifies exceptions to the non-action rule.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Bottleneck-case preapproval and industry designation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In bottleneck cases, pre-approval is not granted until an industry is designated by the Stabilization Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator will not designate an industry except on the recommendation of an interested government agency and only when satisfied that specific standards provided in the regulations have been met. In other words, for bottleneck situations preapproval awaits formal industry designation and satisfaction of regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for measuring allowable cost-of-living increases (53% / 33% rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: In acting upon wage rate increases to compensate for rise in the cost of living, the wage or salary stabilization agency will use specified percentage figures derived from the increase in the cost of living between January 1941 and September 1945.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations specify using 53 percent as the percentage increase in cost of living between January 1941 and September 1945. A 33 percent figure will be applied where the percentage increase in average straight-time hourly earnings in the appropriate unit of employees since January 1941 has not equaled the percentage increase in the cost of living between those dates. The Department of Labor advised that these figures most accurately reflect the increase in cost of living for that period.
